subject: Integration next steps: SDK auth, routing, JSON schema & retry patterns
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@nimbleops.com>, Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and concrete asks so we can keep momentum. Appreciate Alyssa and Tom walking us through the NimbleOps use case (data routing across EU/US, per-tenant embeddings, and a reranker stage for candidate scoring).

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: reliable structured output for downstream processing (order confirmations, attribute extraction) with predictable latency under 300ms p50 for single-request inferencing.
- Core integration items we discussed: SDK onboarding, token-based auth with key rotation, routing policies for region-aware inference, embeddings + reranker flow, and a JSON schema + validation + retry strategy.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
1) Confirm the engineering owners who will join the technical workshop (we suggested Tom + one engineer).
2) Share any current JSON schema examples for the order-confirmation payload you want returned by the model. Even a single example is fine.
3) Any constraints around PII/data retention or KMS requirements (we note HIPAA not required, but you mentioned 7-year retention controls).

Attachments: nimbleops-initial-arch.pdf (diagram), nimbleops-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Next steps we propose:
- Tech workshop (60m) to go through sample prompts, schema constraints (constrained decoding + sentinel tokens), and retry behaviours — proposed slots Thu-Fri this week.
- Redwood to provide an SDK sandbox snippet for quick auth + sample request that returns structured JSON.

If that all sounds right, I’ll lock a time and invite the right engineers.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alyssa Park <alyssa@nimbleops.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Thanks Marcus — quick clarifications from our side:
- I’ll be the technical owner and can bring our backend engineer (Sara).
- Example of the JSON payload we’d like: minimal order confirmation with line items, amount, tax, and a canonical product_id. I’m attaching a small JSON example inline below.

Inline example (abbrev):
{
  "order_id": "ORD-99877",
  "items": [{"product_id": "SKU-123", "qty": 2}],
  "total": 129.98,
  "currency": "USD"
}

A few questions:
- For constrained decoding, do you recommend schema-first (generate only fields defined) or post-hoc validation with retries? We want a low-latency approach that still guarantees strict typing for downstream systems.
- On auth, we need client-side key rotation and integration with our internal Vault. Can Redwood accept short-lived tokens exchanged via our OIDC flow?

I’m available Thu 10-11am PT or Fri afternoon for the workshop.

Tom
Lead Engineer, NimbleOps
tgreene@nimbleops.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alyssa Park <alyssa@nimbleops.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Great to meet you both — I’ll join the workshop from product to cover SLAs and the mutual action plan items. A couple of notes ahead of the workshop:
- For low-latency strict outputs we typically pair constrained decoding (to reduce malformed outputs) with lightweight schema validation on the client and a single automatic retry for schema failures. That pattern keeps p50 latency low while dramatically reducing downstream rejects.
- For embeddings + reranker: we recommend storing tenant embeddings in region-aligned buckets and using a reranker model hosted on dedicated capacity for consistent latency; we can show concrete throughput numbers in the workshop.

I’ll also upload a one-page playbook for the workshop to the Drive link Marcus mentioned.

—Marissa
Director, Product | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Adding a couple of operational checks we should cover in the workshop:
- Routing policy: need to confirm which requests must stay in EU vs which can fallback to US in failover cases. Will NimbleOps accept a soft-fail (best-effort EU) with region flag in payload?
- Observability: we’ll enable token-level tracing for latency/cost breakdowns — Tom, please confirm if you have constraints on sampling.
- Retry semantics: propose idempotency key per request + max 1 automatic retry on schema validation failures. If retry also fails, send to dead-letter queue for manual inspection.

I’ll add these as agenda bullets to the shared workshop doc.

Tessa
Solutions Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

From: Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Thanks — answers inline:
- We need strict EU residency for any Personally Identifiable Data. Non-PII can fallback to US if EU capacity is constrained, but we’d prefer an explicit routing flag in the request so we can control behavior per-tenant.
- Sampling: keep tracing low (1%) for production; higher for sandbox.
- Idempotency key: yes we can adopt that. For the DLQ, can Redwood surface a simple CSV export or a Drive folder we can pull from?

Also, we’ll need a short-lived-token flow: our auth team wants to exchange an OIDC assertion to get short-lived Redwood tokens. Is that supported?

We can do Fri 2026-09-10 09:00 PT for the workshop. Sara (our backend) will join.

Tom
Tom Greene
Lead Engineer, NimbleOps

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <tgreene@nimbleops.com>, Alyssa Park <alyssa@nimbleops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (SDK/auth/routing/schema)

Perfect — I’ve scheduled the 60m workshop for Fri 2026-09-10 at 09:00 PT and shared the calendar invite. Agenda (high level):
- 0-10m: quick introductions + success criteria
- 10-30m: live run of SDK request (auth exchange, region flag, idempotency key) and sample responses
- 30-45m: structured-output strategy (constrained decoding, sentinel tokens, lightweight client-side validation + single retry)
- 45-55m: embeddings + reranker architecture (region residency, dedicated capacity option)
- 55-60m: action items and mutual action plan alignment

Links: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company.net/deal/D-2026-091-NO and shared drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cSharedWorkshopDoc

Action items I’ll take before the call:
- Drop a short SDK sandbox snippet demonstrating OIDC -> short-lived token exchange and a sample structured request.
- Populate the MAP sheet with target success criteria and owners.

Tom/Alyssa — if anything needs to shift for the agenda please reply and we’ll adjust. Looking forward to it.

Regards,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
